result.title: Just-in-Time Skill Retrieval via Long-Horizon State Tracking
result.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly rely on external skill libraries to support complex task execution. However, determining which skills are needed remains challenging in long-horizon tasks. Existing methods typically select a fixed skill set before execution, implicitly assuming that a task's procedural requirements can be determined from its initial description. This assumption is restrictive for long-horizon interaction, where new requirements emerge from intermediate observations, execution outcomes, and newly revealed constraints. This motivates just-in-time skill retrieval, which dynamically selects skills as execution unfolds. Just-in-time skill retrieval is promising but challenging: the utility of a skill depends not only on the current context, but also on the evolving task state shaped by prior steps. To this end, we propose JitSkill, a state-grounded framework that addresses this challenge through continuous task-state tracking. By connecting emerging requirements with accumulated task progress, JitSkill provides procedural support throughout execution without treating each retrieval decision independently. Experiments across three agent benchmarks demonstrate its effectiveness in improving long-horizon task completion. Our code is available at https://github.com/XMUDeepLIT/JitSkill.git/.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文针对长程 LLM agent 任务提出 JitSkill：在执行过程中持续跟踪任务状态，并据此动态检索外部技能，而非在执行前一次性选定固定技能集，并在三个 agent 基准上验证了长程任务完成度的提升。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「依执行进程累积状态、再据状态决定何时获取何种支持」的思路，可能为 LVR 中 LOOK/STOP 的时序决策与支持组合提供概念类比，可供核查状态表示是否可作为 latent 推理的工作区；但该工作面向 agent 技能检索、不涉及视觉或多模态状态，联系较远。
